question: How do embedder size, chunk size, the reranker and hybrid search, and their interactions, change retrieval quality on FinanceBench, FreshStack LangChain (full public corpus), BioASQ and Legal RAG Bench (exploratory) with pinned local models, and how does chunk size change answer faithfulness and correctness at the embedder and reranker sizes chosen on half A? preregistration.md governs (amendment A5).
decision: The first fellowship paper cites these numbers; the experiment changes no production default, and any setting change it suggests goes to a separate proposal.

hypotheses.statement: within scope S (preregistration.md section 2), a bigger embedder ranks gold units higher: rows 1 (4B minus 0.6B) and 2 (8B minus 4B), nDCG@10, directional; a step holds when its row counts on at least 2 of 3 core datasets; H1 holds in full when both steps hold, in part when one does
within scope S (preregistration.md section 2), the reranker raises nDCG@10: row 3 (mean of the three reranker sizes minus off), directional; holds when row 3 counts on at least 2 of 3 core datasets
within scope S (preregistration.md section 2), hybrid search raises nDCG@10: row 4 (hybrid on minus off), directional; holds as H2

within scope S (preregistration.md section 2), reranker plus hybrid beats each alone (simple effects, not an interaction test): rows 5 (both on minus reranker only) and 6 (both on minus hybrid only), nDCG@10, directional; holds on a dataset when both rows count there, and overall on at least 2 of 3 core datasets; the interaction is reported descriptively with its interval
within scope S (preregistration.md section 2), a bigger reranker ranks better: rows 7 (4B minus 0.6B) and 8 (8B minus 4B), reranker-on setups, nDCG@10, directional; holds as H1

within scope S (preregistration.md section 2), chunk size changes retrieval: rows 9 (1,024 minus 512) and 10 (2,048 minus 1,024), two-sided; endpoint evidence_recall_20k on FinanceBench (a stored chunk covers its one page) and nDCG@10 on FreshStack; holds when the same row (9 or 10) counts with the same sign on FinanceBench and on FreshStack; opposite signs are reported as a dataset-dependent effect; BioASQ is a sanity check and Legal RAG Bench is exploratory

within scope S (preregistration.md section 2), a bigger embedder gains more from bigger chunks: row 11, (8B at 2,048 minus 8B at 512) minus (0.6B at 2,048 minus 0.6B at 512), marginal over reranker and hybrid, directional, on the H6 endpoints; a difference of differences with coefficients +1, -1, -1, +1 on those four cells; holds when row 11 counts on both FinanceBench and FreshStack; BioASQ is a sanity check and Legal RAG Bench is exploratory; expected to be underpowered
hypotheses.null: the difference of differences is zero

hypotheses.statement: within scope S (preregistration.md section 2), chunk size changes GLM-5.3 faithfulness on factual claims and Ragas AnswerCorrectness in the 12 crossed setups, where context length grows with chunk size: rows 12 to 13 (faithfulness) and 14 to 15 (correctness), 1,024 minus 512 and 2,048 minus 1,024, marginal over reranker and hybrid, two-sided, all questions, 3 runs averaged per question; per outcome, holds when the same row counts with the same sign on FinanceBench and on FreshStack; BioASQ rows are sanity checks; faithfulness is expected to fall as chunks grow; Legal RAG Bench is exploratory; FinanceBench number match is secondary; confirmatory

within scope S (preregistration.md section 2), chunk size changes faithfulness and correctness at a fixed pre-assembly evidence budget of 20,480 Qwen3 tokens of stored chunks (the cut total): rows 16 to 17 (faithfulness) and 18 to 19 (correctness), c1024-t20k minus c512-t20k and c2048-t20k minus c1024-t20k, two-sided, at reranker on and hybrid on with the chosen sizes (conditional on that cell); holds as H8a (same row, same sign, on FinanceBench and on FreshStack); H8b fixes the pre-assembly budget, not the model-visible evidence, so it does not separate chunk size from context length; 'chunk size changes X at a fixed pre-assembly evidence budget' is claimed only when H8b holds for outcome X and the registered sensitivity on questions where all three -t20k setups reach a cut total (the kept stored chunks, before assembly) of at least 19,456 tokens (95% of 20,480) gives the sign of the row's H8b result on FinanceBench and on FreshStack (a sign reversed on either dataset is disagreement); every question stays in H8b; realised (assembled) evidence token totals are recorded per question and setup and reported per setup beside each H8b result; confirmatory

decision_rule: preregistration.md sections 7 to 9 govern. No mixed model. For row k and question q, the contrast score d_qk is the mean of q's scores over the cells at the first level minus the mean over the cells at the second level (equal cell weights; answer scores averaged over 3 runs first); this recipe does not apply to row 11 (H7): each of its four corner cells is first averaged over reranker and hybrid, then d_q11 = (+1) e8b-c2048 (-1) e8b-c512 (-1) e0.6b-c2048 (+1) e0.6b-c512, so scores 0.8, 0.2, 0.3, 0.7 give 1.0, and its estimate, interval and MDE use that scale (known-answer fixture case); the estimate is the plain mean of d_qk over questions. FreshStack, BioASQ and Legal: the decision test is defined by its closed form (preregistration.md section 9 point 3): estimate = mean of d_qk; variance = sum of squared residuals x (n / (n minus 1)) squared / n squared (Mancl and DeRouen bias-reduced sandwich, intercept only, one row per cluster); t reference on n minus 1 degrees of freedom for the p-value and interval. Implementation: statsmodels GEE (version 0.15.0, `stats` dependency group, recorded in uv.lock) of d_qk on an intercept (Gaussian, identity link, independence working correlation, clusters = questions, cov_type bias_reduced); a known-answer test checks it against the closed form, and the closed form is used if they differ. The closed form was checked against statsmodels 0.15.0 on 2026-11-14 and matched to 1e-10. FinanceBench: the decision p-value and 95% interval come from a document-level sign-flip permutation test (100,000 draws, seed 20261101). Holm (alpha 0.05) within families fixed now: FinanceBench 19 rows, FreshStack 19 rows, BioASQ 8 rows (rows 1 to 8; rows 9 to 19 are sanity checks); Legal RAG Bench has no family and is exploratory. A row whose measure fails its gate, or that the differential-error rule makes exploratory, stays in its family with p = 1 and is reported as not testable. A directional row counts when the Holm-adjusted p is below 0.05 and the estimate has the predicted sign; a two-sided row counts when the Holm-adjusted p is below 0.05. Hypotheses hold by the rule in each statement (H1 to H5: 2 of 3 core datasets; H6, H7, H8a and H8b: FinanceBench and FreshStack). A two-sided hypothesis needs the same sign: under the both-datasets rule (H6, H8a, H8b) the row counts with the same sign on FinanceBench and FreshStack, and opposite signs are reported as a dataset-dependent effect and the hypothesis does not hold; under a 2-of-3 rule (Part 2 C1 and C2) the row counts with the same sign on at least 2 of the 3 core datasets, and an opposite-sign count on the third is reported as a dataset-dependent effect and does not stop the hypothesis holding. Fixed search settings: similarity_threshold 0.0, metadata extraction disabled, exact dense search with no approximate vector index, chunk overlap 15% (77, 154 and 307 tokens). Search scoring: top 100 stored chunks, taken before OMRS context assembly (rerank pool 100, fetch_k 100), collapsed to distinct units and cut at 10; on FinanceBench each stored chunk has one page label and covers that page, for nDCG@10 and evidence_recall_20k alike; a chunk with no page label or no corpus unit maps to a placeholder unit that keeps its rank and is not relevant. Registered sensitivity checks, never decisive: paired permutation by question (10,000 shuffles, seed 20261101) on FreshStack and BioASQ; GEE with document clusters on FinanceBench (t on documents minus 1). A non-significant result means no difference was detected; there is no equivalence claim and no TOST.
baseline: none: full factorial of embedder x chunk size x reranker x hybrid (72 search setups per dataset); e4b-c1024-roff-hoff is the reference cell of the G2 rebuild check only
candidate: 72 search setups e<0.6b|4b|8b>-c<512|1024|2048>-r<off|0.6b|4b|8b>-h<off|on>; 15 answer setups (12 crossed plus token-matched c512-t20k, c1024-t20k and c2048-t20k; the third added by A3), chosen on half A, at the embedder and reranker sizes chosen by the pre-registered selection rule (pooled over the three core datasets, amendment A3); index cost and configuration hash as defined in preregistration.md section 14.1

weighted share on 100 L1 test pod session claims (2026-11-23, pre-freeze)

amendments.summary: Full-factorial redesign agreed with the operator before the freeze. Replaces the six one-factor arms (documents-profile-4b, embedding-0.6b, embedding-8b, reranker-off, chunking-off, hybrid) with embedder (0.6B, 4B, 8B) x chunk size (512, 1024, 2048, overlap 15%) x reranker (off, Qwen3-Reranker 0.6B, 4B, 8B) x hybrid (off, BM25 on): 72 search setups per dataset. Adds Legal RAG Bench (100 questions, exploratory) and uses the 203 public FreshStack queries (was 223). Drops MiniLM, the chunking-off arm, Granite Guardian (runtime entry judge-granite-guardian removed) and hypothesis H-CC. Hypotheses H1 to H7 (search) and H8 (answer stage) replace the five per-arm hypotheses. Answer stage: 12 setups at the embedder and reranker sizes chosen by a pre-registered rule, 3 runs each. Budget: the $250 cap is replaced by an estimate of about $555 and a ceiling of $830. The three Qwen3-Reranker GGUF files are pinned in the runtime block after the test pod check (Exp 35 task 4A.3). One GPU type for every main-run pod, chosen before the freeze from a fixed timing job on RTX 4090, L40S and H100 by the rule in protocol.md section 0.8a; the 9 indexes build on parallel pods of that type.

amendments.summary: Publication review fixes F1 to F30, approved by the operator on 2026-11-14, and the second-round fixes C1 to C24 ruled on the same day. From A4 on, preregistration.md governs the live design and wins over protocol.md, this file and the OpenSpec changes; earlier amendments are history. Hypotheses: H1 to H7 scoped (scope S) with numbered rows and a holds rule each; H4 named as simple effects; H6, H7, H8a and H8b hold only on FinanceBench and FreshStack (H8a and H8b: open item O6, decided by the operator on 2026-11-14), and a two-sided hypothesis needs the same row with the same sign on every dataset its rule needs; H8 split into H8a (12 crossed setups) and H8b (3 token-matched setups), both confirmatory; every null is a zero effect; Legal RAG Bench exploratory everywhere, H8a and H8b correctness included. Analysis: the mixed model is dropped; per-question contrast scores with an intercept-only GEE (bias-reduced covariance, t on G minus 1) on FreshStack, BioASQ and Legal, and a document-level sign-flip test (100,000 draws, seed 20261101) on FinanceBench; Holm families fixed at 19 (FinanceBench), 19 (FreshStack) and 8 (BioASQ; rows 9 to 19 are sanity checks there), 46 contrasts; a gated row stays in its family with p = 1. Metrics: nDCG@10 is the primary metric of the study; evidence_recall_20k is the confirmatory endpoint for H6 and H7 on FinanceBench (rows 9 to 11) with any-page credit, so both carry primary: true in metrics (first-page credit is a sensitivity); alpha-nDCG@10 is secondary on FreshStack if its nugget labels allow (P3). FreshStack: all 9 indexes rebuilt on the full public LangChain corpus (49,514 documents, pinned revision, P1); the 10,000-document subset is retired. Labels and gates: L1 750 (claim kinds 100, faithfulness 450 at 150 per chunk size from answers to all questions, correctness 200 at 50 per dataset), L2 750 in the full plan (every item L1 labels and every Part 2 label), or 365 at the staged fallback's first stage (a seeded 30% of the faithfulness and claim-kind sets, with the rest of a set added when kappa on its subset is below 0.70 overall or, for faithfulness, within any chunk-size level, or is undefined; O4); faithfulness gate per checker (pooled over the core datasets) and correctness gate per core dataset on kappa point estimate (at least 0.60) and lower 95% bound (at least 0.40), plus an AUC check on the continuous correctness score; every gate interval a percentile bootstrap with 10,000 resamples by question and its own seed; differential-error rule on GLM-5.3 in either direction; a length-controlled check on 300 claims. Runs: two closed-book runs (own-knowledge prompt, and the RAG prompt with empty evidence) beside the oracle run; H8a and H8b correctness rows re-run on questions both closed-book runs answer wrongly. Halves and order: FinanceBench split by document, the other datasets by question (seed 20261115); score half A, write selection.json, time-stamp the A3 configuration hash on OSF (O1, decided by the owner on 2026-11-14), then score half B; the RQ1 retrieval headline is the A3 cell on half B. Selection terms: index cost is stored vector values (chunks times embedding dimension) summed over the three core datasets; the configuration hash is the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the selected cell's resolved settings plus the halves.json SHA-256. The openai/gpt-6.1-terra cross-check is removed, because no cost estimate included it; its reference entry is deleted. New seeds 20261118 (pilot), 20261119 (length-controlled check) and 20261121 to 20261135 (smoke sample, L2 subsets used only in the staged plan, gate bootstraps, RAGFlow samples, Part 2 labels; preregistration.md section 16) wait for confirmation (P9); 20261120 (audit) is used only if the O3 unjudged-share trigger fires; 20261124 is retired. Budget: estimate about $730 plus the pilot (the full FreshStack build is not timed yet, P2; the pilot cost is projected from P2 and approved before the pod starts), ceiling $975 unchanged. Results-blind drop order at the ceiling: (1) Legal RAG Bench answer generation, (2) the length-controlled check, (3) the closed-book run with the RAG prompt, then stop; E1 has its own ceiling; a run that finishes every confirmatory item after drops is complete with registered drops, each a numbered deviation; no operator choice. Part 2 and E1 get their own estimate and ceiling (P16). The frozen list stays empty until the freeze; the pins table in preregistration.md section 16 fills it (answer-model host, reasoning mode, output cap and context length; judge, classifier and GLM-5.3 settings; query instruction, reranker instruction and hybrid settings; FreshStack and Legal revisions; halves.json and prompt template hashes; the evidence_recall_20k tolerance; the freeze commit and OSF link). These are pre-freeze tasks P1 to P16 and are not filled here; no owner decision is open. After the freeze, every change is a dated, numbered deviation, added to this list and uploaded to OSF. CodeRabbit round 1 on PR 210 (2026-11-14, before the freeze): faithfulness_glm_factual is named as faithfulness of cited factual claims; uncited_segment_share is a co-outcome, and a registered sensitivity counts uncited factual segments as unsupported (O7, decided by the owner on 2026-11-14: the primary measure stays faithfulness of cited factual claims, and the uncited version stays a sensitivity analysis only); undefined gate statistics fail closed (preregistration.md section 11.2); the run stops early only on preflight, G1 to G3 or the ceiling after the last drop step, and a failed outcome-validation gate leaves its rows not testable; the 2-of-3 same-sign rule is stated once for C1 and C2; Part 2 C2 uses complete pairs with a sensitivity that scores unjudged rows 0; the half-B guard checks the hash of the current selection file. Owner decisions of 2026-11-14: O1, a file upload to the registered OSF project time-stamps the A3 configuration hash; O5, no ethics query, because the study has no human participants and every labeller is an author or colleague (a paid external annotator reopens the question as a deviation); O7, the primary faithfulness measure stays cited factual claims, because OMRS answers are built to cite their evidence; O2, SESOI 0.02 nDCG@10 with a written justification (preregistration.md section 10), recorded before any pilot result is read; O3, no relevance audit unless the mean unjudged share in the top 10 differs by more than 5 points (hybrid on against off on FreshStack, or OMRS against RAGFlow on a core dataset in Part 2), a trigger defined only on datasets whose qrels list judged non-relevant units, while for positives-only datasets the owner decides at P4 between a fixed small audit and no audit; O4 (revised the same day), L2 is an author or colleague and labels every item L1 labels and every Part 2 label (L1 750 and L2 750, or 700 each after drop step 1); only if L2 cannot commit the time, a staged fallback labels a seeded 30% of the faithfulness and claim-kind sets first (L2 365, or 315 after drop step 1) and the rest of a set when kappa on its subset is below 0.70 overall or, for faithfulness, within any chunk-size level, or is undefined; the plan is chosen and dated before the freeze from L2's availability alone, and the name goes in the run record only. CodeRabbit round 2 (PR 210): row 11 (H7) uses coefficients +1, -1, -1, +1 on its four corner cells, and its MDE uses that scale; every question stays in H8b, realised evidence token totals are recorded per question and setup, and 'chunk size itself' also needs the registered sensitivity on questions where all three -t20k setups reach at least 95% of 20,480 tokens; every undefined resample is left out (or takes its chance value) and counted once, separately from the over-5% failure rule; if drop step 1 applies, no Legal correctness answer is drawn (correctness 150, L1 700, L2 700 in the full plan or 315 at the staged first stage, after O4; no confirmatory row changes).

amendments.summary: Harness review rulings (findings H-01 to H-36, questions Q1 to Q17, fact check F1 to F6), approved by the owner on 2026-11-14. Defines terms the pre-registration left open and records implementation rules; no hypothesis, Holm family, gate threshold, budget, drop order or label count changes. Chunk: a stored chunk (one index row as written at ingest); scoring, the 100-chunk depth, evidence_recall_20k and the 20,480-token cut use the top 100 stored chunks taken before OMRS context assembly, through one additive OMRS search option (default off). Answer stage: head of that list (10 chunks, or the token cut on stored chunks), then assembly of the kept whole chunks with no neighbour expansion, a truncated crossing chunk kept as its own item, then Engine.answer with rows=; cut total and realised evidence token total both recorded, and the H8b 95% sensitivity filter uses the cut total (an orchestrator choice flagged to the owner, protocol.md section 0.14 item 25). FinanceBench: each stored chunk has one page label, so 'a chunk covers its page' replaces the first-page and any-page rules, and the page-rule sensitivity analyses that become identical by construction are removed, and one H6 FinanceBench sensitivity stays (nDCG@10 with a chunk covering its page, sign agreement reported per row against the endpoint); evidence_recall_20k stays the H6 and H7 FinanceBench endpoint; chunks with no page label are refused at the seal and, like unmapped chunks, map to a counted placeholder unit that keeps its rank and is not relevant. FreshStack export: row text only, IDs, URLs and byte offsets in a manifest, .md and .mdx unchanged, every other row in a backtick fence one longer than its longest backtick run (at least three), with a no-fence fallback; query is title, blank line, body. Search stage saves lists and timings only and computes no metric; a separate scorer runs per half. G1: each answer run saves its 100 stored chunk IDs and is compared with the matching search setup's single run; evidence equals the list head; a failed side is incomplete, never a match. Resend rule: an error row is not a result; failed answer, search, local-checker and Ragas calls are resent on --resume; returned content is final; a call with 3 errors that are not rate limit or out-of-credit is closed as missing; resent_calls counts harness-level resends only (client-library retries stated as a limitation). Statistics: gate percentile bounds at zero-based indexes 250 and 9,749 of 10,000 sorted resamples; 'within 0.01' means gap <= 0.01 + 1e-9 on unrounded pooled scores; FinanceBench GEE sensitivity uses t on documents minus 1; sign-flip interval ends by bisection to 0.0001 on the same 100,000 draws, 1e-12 tie tolerance registered; zero estimate and zero variance gives p = 1, a NaN p-value raises before Holm. Seed 20261101 gains two local uses (question order, smoke corpus sample). Clef-Flash server arguments aligned at P10 with the LLM-AggreFact preset; Ragas adapter text hashed under P13; passage files prepared once with a tree hash; budget-check.json and drops.json; main stage refuses an unfrozen plan or dirty tree, run record holds the preregistration.md SHA-256; released answers in a separate folder with identifier rules only. New pre-freeze tasks P17 (reproduce the router idle stop on the test pod) and P18 (correct the protocol.md section 4.4 overflow sentence against the saved score files). PR 211 review (protocol.md section 0.14 items 26 to 31): H8b is a comparison at a fixed pre-assembly evidence budget and does not separate chunk size from context length, with the realised token total per setup reported beside it; an answer closed as missing scores 0 for correctness, is not judged and stays in the complete cases, while the unjudged-row and Part 2 C2 rules apply only to an existing answer whose judge call was closed; a pre-freeze run appends its line to output/run-records.jsonl with prefreeze: true, which the join and main-run checks ignore; the FreshStack export keeps the published row text byte for byte apart from the fence; the no-page-label placeholder applies on FinanceBench only; the search stage also saves each ranked chunk's pinned Qwen3 token count (no chunk text), and the scorer computes evidence_recall_20k from these counts. Build review (protocol.md section 0.14 items 32 to 43, 2026-11-17): random generators and orders of the halves, sign-flip and permutation tests written down; BioASQ and Legal use nDCG@10 for rows 9 to 11; sensitivity p-values get Holm in the same family and are shown unadjusted and adjusted, and no confirmatory claim rests on them; MDE uses the sample SD and a design effect floored at 1; configuration hash field halves_sha256; FinanceBench number match counts a lone year as a number and does not score a reference with no number (denominator stated); ceiling reached at $975 or more, billing rows {provider, usd}; reranker failure (HTTP error, 600 s timeout, bad reply) saves no row; classifier gate sample and scoring rules, refusal regular expression pinned by SHA-256 under P13; refusal rate is a share of claims with question-bootstrap intervals and new seed 20261136 (owner to confirm, P9); correctness AUC under both can't-tell treatments; faithfulness gate pool holds fact, mixed and unclassified claims only. PR 211 review (item 44): a smoke run appends one run-record line with smoke: true, ignored like prefreeze lines.
